answer: Bonded cargo travels under a customs seal that only the officer may break, and the seal number is kept in the customs book from quay to warehouse. A velvet seal cut in the night fails the book: the beacon of the warehouse must hold the seal the officer issued, and a broken seal means the cargo was opened. Forging the seal means bribing a customs officer, faking 150 seal numbers and paying 29,700, while the marble entry in the customs book is read at every delivery, so cargo whose seal was never entered is seized at the gate.
